speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly when your double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness started, and whether these symptoms worsen with fatigue or exercise.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fact that your double vision occurs specifically with upward or downward gaze, and your weakness fluctuates with activity, strongly suggests a neuromuscular issue. Do you experience drooping eyelids (ptosis) or have noticed any slurred speech or difficulty chewing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: No recent infections or family history, and symmetrical weakness, help narrow this down. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, speaking clearly, or holding your head upright against gravity? REQUEST TEST: Muscle_ENzyme_panel; REQUEST TEST: Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal results from the muscle enzyme and nerve stimulation tests make myasthenia gravis less likely, so have you noticed any improvement in your double vision or weakness when you close your eyes or look down? REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR_Antibody; REQUEST TEST: Edrophonium_Test.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-AChR_Antibody: Present (elevated); Edrophonium_Test: Positive (significant improvement in ptosis and diplopia noted)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of Anti-AChR antibodies combined with a positive Edrophonium test, along with your history of fluctuating weakness and gaze-dependent diplopia, confirms this diagnosis.
